caseStudies.title: Messenger Archive & Semantic Search
caseStudies.problem: Long-running personal chat archives combine text and voice messages across thousands of threads, making keyword search ineffective for recalling context or supplying structured history to LLM agents.
caseStudies.context: Self-directed personal engineering project built independently outside employer work to explore Rust/Python interoperability, local speech-to-text, vector indexing, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling.
caseStudies.architecture: A Rust sync service fetches personal chat history over MTProto with flood-wait backoff into PostgreSQL. A Python worker claims pending voice rows using PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED and transcribes them with Whisper. A Rust indexer computes batched local embeddings and upserts points into Qdrant, exposed to LLM agents via a read-only MCP server (stdio and HTTP).
challenges: No distributed transaction spans PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and the sync cursor checkpoint.
Respecting upstream MTProto rate limits while recovering cleanly from mid-batch interruptions.
decisions: Computed deterministic UUIDv5 Qdrant point IDs from message identity so retries overwrite idempotently instead of creating duplicates.
Persisted the indexing checkpoint only after each Qdrant upsert batch succeeds.
Used PostgreSQL SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for lock-free concurrent voice transcription workers.
reliability: At-least-once processing paired with deterministic UUIDv5 upserts delivers idempotent eventual consistency without 2PC.
Flood-wait backoff and bounded retries protect upstream API sessions.
results: End-to-end personal archive searchable semantically across text and transcribed voice messages through standard MCP clients.

caseStudies.title: EntityLocker — Row-Level Entity Concurrency Utility
caseStudies.problem: Applications caching or mutating domain entities concurrently often face either coarse global locks that bottleneck throughput or complex ad-hoc per-key lock maps prone to leaks and races.
caseStudies.context: Public open-source Java library demonstrating fine-grained JVM concurrency primitives comparable to row-level database locking.
caseStudies.architecture: A generic EntityLocker<ID> coordinator manages per-entity-ID mutual exclusion without coupling to entity payload types, supporting different ID types, reentrant locking semantics, escalation/global locking options, and bounded cleanup of unused lock entries.
challenges: Preventing race conditions between lock acquisition, reference counting, and map eviction when locks are released.
Supporting arbitrary generic ID types safely without deadlocks or unbounded memory growth.
decisions: Decoupled lock coordination completely from entity storage so components only pass primary key identifiers.
Used concurrent map atomic operations and reference tracking to reclaim idle lock objects safely.
reliability: Isolates contention to the specific entity ID being mutated rather than blocking unrelated entities.
Avoids memory leaks under high key cardinality via safe lock entry cleanup.
results: Published as a standalone reusable Java utility on GitHub (stden/EntityLocker).

architectureDiagrams.title: Semantic Search & MCP Integration
architectureDiagrams.label: Independent personal project architecture: MTProto sync service in Rust, PostgreSQL queue, Python Whisper worker, batched Rust indexer, Qdrant vector DB, and MCP server
architectureDiagrams.summary: Cross-language personal ingestion pipeline bridging PostgreSQL and Qdrant with idempotent UUIDv5 upserts and read-only MCP tool exposure.

nodes.title: Messenger API (MTProto)
nodes.responsibility: Provides incremental message history and voice attachments subject to upstream rate limits.
nodes.tradeoffs: Rate-limited upstream API requires persistent cursor checkpoints to avoid costly full re-syncs.

nodes.title: Sync Service (Rust)
nodes.responsibility: Fetches history with exponential/flood-wait backoff and stores raw messages in PostgreSQL.
nodes.tradeoffs: Rust async runtime handles long-running sync sessions with predictable memory footprint.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL Store & Queue
nodes.responsibility: Stores canonical chat records and coordinates voice transcription jobs via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
nodes.tradeoffs: Using PostgreSQL for both storage and job queuing removes an extra broker dependency at personal scale.

nodes.title: Transcription Worker (Python)
nodes.responsibility: Claims un-transcribed voice attachments and writes transcripts back to PostgreSQL.
nodes.tradeoffs: Separating Python ML execution keeps the core Rust sync and indexing paths lightweight.

nodes.title: Batch Indexer (Rust)
nodes.responsibility: Generates local text embeddings in batches and saves the indexing cursor only after upsert confirmation.
nodes.tradeoffs: Checkpoint-after-upsert avoids distributed 2PC transactions across PostgreSQL and Qdrant.

nodes.title: Vector Store (Qdrant)
nodes.responsibility: Stores semantic embeddings keyed by deterministic UUIDv5 identifiers derived from message identity.
nodes.tradeoffs: Deterministic IDs make replay after crash completely safe without duplicate vector entries.

nodes.title: MCP Server (stdio / HTTP)
nodes.responsibility: Exposes semantic search and thread retrieval tools to LLM assistants over Model Context Protocol.
nodes.tradeoffs: Read-only query tools isolate LLM agents from direct database or session credentials.

architectureDiagrams.title: Fine-Grained Entity Concurrency Locking (EntityLocker)
architectureDiagrams.label: Open-source Java library EntityLocker: caller threads, lock registry, per-ID lock entry, protected critical section, and lock reclamation
architectureDiagrams.summary: Public Java concurrency design providing row-level mutual exclusion keyed by entity identifier without blocking unrelated keys.

nodes.title: Concurrent Caller Threads
nodes.responsibility: Multiple application threads contend on reads or mutations identified solely by generic entity IDs.
nodes.tradeoffs: Key-based locking preserves parallelism across distinct entities compared to coarse class-level locks.

nodes.title: Concurrent Lock Registry
nodes.responsibility: Atomically resolves or creates the synchronization entry for a given entity key.
nodes.tradeoffs: Atomic map updates prevent duplicate lock instances for the same key under high contention.

nodes.title: Per-ID Reentrant Lock
nodes.responsibility: Serialises access per entity ID while allowing optional global escalation or lock acquisition timeouts.
nodes.tradeoffs: Timeouts protect caller threads against deadlock or slow downstream operations.

nodes.title: Protected Critical Section
nodes.responsibility: Executes the guarded state update while holding only the target entity's lock.
nodes.tradeoffs: Keeps critical sections short and deterministic to minimise tail latency.

nodes.title: Reference-Safe Eviction
nodes.responsibility: Decrements active waiter counts on unlock and safely removes unreferenced entries from the registry.
nodes.tradeoffs: Careful reference checks prevent evicting an entry while another thread is acquiring it.

architectureDiagrams.originLabel: Independent educational reference architecture — unrelated to any employer system
architectureDiagrams.title: Transactional Outbox & Idempotent Event Consumer
architectureDiagrams.label: Educational reference architecture: application service, relational outbox transaction, outbox relay, message broker, idempotent consumer, and dead-letter queue
architectureDiagrams.summary: Standard educational distributed-systems pattern guaranteeing atomic database writes and reliable at-least-once event publishing.

nodes.title: Domain Service (Java / Spring)
nodes.responsibility: Validates incoming requests and executes domain state transitions inside a single local transaction.
nodes.tradeoffs: Avoids brittle two-phase commit across database and message broker.

nodes.title: Relational DB + Outbox Table
nodes.responsibility: Persists domain state and outbox event payload in the same ACID PostgreSQL transaction.
nodes.tradeoffs: Guarantees no lost events on crash at the cost of small relational write amplification.

nodes.title: Outbox Relay Publisher
nodes.responsibility: Reads unpublished outbox rows and emits events to the message broker with monotonic checkpoints.
nodes.tradeoffs: At-least-once relay requires downstream consumers to handle duplicate deliveries safely.

nodes.title: Message Broker (Kafka / AMQP)
nodes.responsibility: Decouples producers and consumers while buffering spikes and preserving per-key ordering.
nodes.tradeoffs: Partitioning scales throughput horizontally; cross-partition ordering is not global.

nodes.title: Idempotent Consumer
nodes.responsibility: Checks deterministic event ID before applying updates so redelivered events are safe no-ops.
nodes.tradeoffs: Maintaining an idempotency key index trades minor storage overhead for safe retries.

nodes.title: Retry & Dead-Letter Queue
nodes.responsibility: Routes poison payloads after bounded backoff retries to a dead-letter queue for inspection.
nodes.tradeoffs: Prevents malformed messages from stalling healthy partition progress.

architectureDiagrams.originLabel: Independent educational reference architecture — unrelated to any employer system
architectureDiagrams.title: Resilient Asynchronous Job Queue & Backpressure
architectureDiagrams.label: Educational reference architecture: API producer, persistent job queue, bounded worker pool, atomic result staging, and observability metrics
architectureDiagrams.summary: Standard educational pattern for decoupling slow background jobs from synchronous API latency using bounded worker pools and safe retries.

nodes.title: Stateless API Frontend
nodes.responsibility: Authenticates requests, enqueues work asynchronously, and returns a job correlation ID immediately.
nodes.tradeoffs: Keeps request threads fast and predictable instead of blocking on long-running background work.

nodes.title: Persistent Work Queue
nodes.responsibility: Durably tracks queued, in-flight, completed, and failed job states with lease/visibility timeouts.
nodes.tradeoffs: Explicit lease timeouts allow recovery if a worker crashes mid-execution.

nodes.title: Bounded Worker Pool
nodes.responsibility: Executes tasks up to a configured concurrency ceiling to protect downstream CPU, memory, and DB pools.
nodes.tradeoffs: Backpressure caps queue drain rate to prevent cascading overload.

nodes.title: Staged Write & Atomic Commit
nodes.responsibility: Writes output artifacts to staging before marking the job completed so readers never see partial results.
nodes.tradeoffs: Uses brief temporary storage headroom to guarantee clean read consistency.

nodes.title: Health, Metrics & Cleanup
nodes.responsibility: Exports queue lag, retry counts, and purges expired temporary artifacts on a predictable schedule.
nodes.tradeoffs: Scheduled TTL cleanup decouples storage reclamation from user-facing latency.

engineeringConcepts.name: Idempotency
engineeringConcepts.description: Deterministic UUIDv5 vector point IDs in the personal archive pipeline and deduplication keys in the outbox pattern ensure retries overwrite cleanly without duplicates.

engineeringConcepts.name: Eventual Consistency
engineeringConcepts.description: Advancing sync checkpoints only after downstream upserts succeed and committing outbox events alongside domain state keeps distributed stores convergent.

engineeringConcepts.name: Message Delivery Guarantees
engineeringConcepts.description: Pairing durable queues or outbox relays with idempotent consumers turns at-least-once broker delivery into effectively-once domain outcomes.

engineeringConcepts.name: Failure Handling
engineeringConcepts.description: Bounded retries, upstream flood-wait backoff, and dead-letter queues keep transient faults recoverable without halting healthy traffic.

engineeringConcepts.name: Distributed Coordination
engineeringConcepts.description: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED job claiming, per-key lock registries (EntityLocker), and broker partitions coordinate concurrent workers without global locks.

engineeringConcepts.name: Cache Consistency
engineeringConcepts.description: Staged writes before atomic publication and reference-counted lock eviction prevent torn reads or stale cache entries under concurrency.

engineeringConcepts.name: Observability
engineeringConcepts.description: Queue lag metrics, explicit job state machines, dead-letter alerts, and automated quality-gate checks (SonarQubeChecker) keep faults diagnosable.

engineeringConcepts.name: Security
engineeringConcepts.description: Least-privilege read-only MCP interfaces, stateless API input validation, and isolating runtime credentials away from AI agent tool surfaces.
